bullets.title: Global bond yields hit multi-year highs; 30Y at highest since 2007, pressuring risk assets
bullets.body: Global bond yields rose to levels not seen since 2008, with the 30-year Treasury at its highest since 2007. The S&P sold off ~69bps and Nasdaq ~168bps on the move, driven by AI capex-related corporate debt issuance (BofA estimates ~30bps of the 10Y rise attributable to hyperscaler borrowing). The 10Y yield stabilized around 4.65% pre-market Wednesday as Treasury buyback operations were doubled from $2B to $4B per operation, functionally acting as 'QE lite' and helping 30Y yields fall 9bps, 10Y down 6bps.

bullets.title: Treasury's doubled long-end buybacks read as 'Operation Twist 2.0'; positive for risk assets, gold, rate-sensitives
bullets.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent doubled long-end liquidity support operations, consistent with a 2011 Operation Twist playbook. Analysts note the long end appears unable to digest supply from an accelerating fiscal deficit; however, equities are more sensitive to the funds rate path than term premium. The 2011 analog saw materials +21.9%, energy +21.8%, financials +19%, and the S&P rally 15% off lows post-announcement.

bullets.title: S&P correcting from ATHs on decelerating volume; high-beta momentum down 6.4%, healthcare outperforming
bullets.body: SPY has pulled back 3 days from all-time highs on decelerating volume, described as an 'Investable Bucket Vol Regime' rather than a repeat of July's Quad4 sell-off. High-beta momentum names fell 6.4% on Tuesday while healthcare (XLV) gained 1.6%. Retail investor portfolios were down ~4.0% on the day and flat year-to-date despite broader market near records. 458 S&P 500 companies have now reported with aggregate 50% YoY earnings growth.

bullets.title: Asia tech suffers serious puke: KOSPI -5.8% (down 29% from peak), Nikkei -3.2%, ChiNext -7%
bullets.body: South Korea's KOSPI fell another 5.8% overnight after breaking a key technical support level, now down 29% from recent highs. Japan's Nikkei fell 3.2%, breaking Hedgeye TRADE signal support for the second time in two months. China's ChiNext fell 6% and STAR 50 fell 7%, with broad Asia tech weakness. SK Hynix announced a buyback following the Kospi plunge.

bullets.title: AI capex increasingly debt-financed; rising 10Y yields could pressure marginal project economics
bullets.body: AI-related debt could reach $7.1 trillion, shifting buildout financing from hyperscaler cash flows to debt-dependent lenders directly sensitive to long-term rates. One-month rolling beta between AI infrastructure baskets and 10Y yields has paradoxically flipped positive, possibly reflecting stronger nominal growth expectations rather than financing cost concerns; the 6-month correlation remains negative. BofA estimates AI corporate debt issuance contributed ~30bps to this year's 10Y yield rise.

bullets.title: Data center regulatory headwinds intensifying: PA enacts 'strictest guardrails in nation,' other states following
bullets.body: Pennsylvania Governor Shapiro enacted an executive order removing AI data center projects from fast-track permitting and barring NDA use, calling it the strictest such regulation nationally. Regulatory pressure is spreading across TX, OH, and GA, with both Democratic and Republican gubernatorial candidates in Ohio opposing or seeking to further regulate data centers. PJM Interconnection is also seeking FERC approval to require data centers provide their own power or face curtailments, while Texas faces record grid demand >91GW.

bullets.title: AI power scarcity is the critical bottleneck: time-to-power trumps pricing, 2027 delivery key
bullets.body: Multiple sources — NVDA, INTC, GFS management, and PSP operators — confirm a power-constrained environment as the critical bottleneck for AI datacenter scaling. Customers are actively requesting more power urgently, with 2027 power delivery the top priority in hyperscaler negotiations. Power scarcity is expected to increase the value of existing power positions as grid access becomes harder and more expensive. Behind-the-meter generation is more complex at scale than on-grid solutions.

bullets.title: Midterm election framework: AI governance and data center policy emerging as central electoral issues
bullets.body: A research framework assigns 75% probability to a House-D/Senate-R base case, which would favor consumer staples, healthcare, and financials while creating headwinds for info tech and legacy energy. AI governance (safety, IP, accountability) and data center resource utilization are rising sharply in public policy sentiment, with Senate campaigns actively positioning on data center concerns. Treasury is adding long-end liquidity ahead of elections, consistent with historical pre-election macro policy patterns.

bullets.title: Hedgeye macro regime: USD bearish, long EUR/JPY, long gold vs. short USD as alpha trade
bullets.body: Hedgeye's McCullough maintains short USD, long Euros (FXE) and Yens (FXY), and long gold (AAAU) as core positioning, noting it is a 'rarity in 27 years' to be long both EUR and JPY simultaneously. Long Gold vs. Short USD is identified as the outperforming alpha trade over long bitcoin. McCullough also added VXF, IVOL, JEDI, and IGV while reducing EWZ, healthcare ETFs, and equal-weight exposure.

bullets.title: Import/export price inflation decelerating but remains elevated; housing and mortgage data soft
bullets.body: July import prices rose 5.9% YoY (down from 6.7% prior), export prices +8.2% YoY (down from 10.0%), suggesting sequential deceleration but persistent inflation. Pending home sales fell 2.5% YoY in July, moving negative for first time since January, with all four regions declining. MBA mortgage applications fell 0.4% for the week of Aug 14 (vs. +3.6% prior), with 30-year rates unchanged at 6.77%. Architecture billings remained in contraction at 46.6 (from 47.3 in June). Hedgeye CPI Nowcast projects 11bps acceleration in headline CPI YoY on Sept 11.

bullets.title: NY Fed Services PMI shows double-digit deterioration in August; 6-month expectations turn pessimistic
bullets.body: The NY Fed Services PMI showed double-digit month-over-month declines in both business activity and business climate components in August. Six-month forward expectations also moved more pessimistic, adding to the macro uncertainty picture alongside soft housing data and decelerating trade price inflation.

bullets.title: TGT beats strongly with +3.8% comps and raises FY guidance; $994M tariff refund boosts Q2
bullets.body: Target reported Q2 comp sales of +3.8% vs. consensus +2.43%, driven by traffic growth of +3.6%; net sales of $26.54B beat estimates. Q2 net income of $1.877B crushed IBES estimate of $1.061B, partly aided by $994M pretax tariff refund benefit in gross margin. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $9.90–$10.90. However, comps decelerated ~180bps from Q1's +5.6%, and the bar heading into H2 is now higher.

bullets.title: TJX Q2 beats but Marmaxx comps decelerate 500bps to +1%; guidance disappoints; stock lower
bullets.body: TJX reported Q2 comps of +4.0% beating consensus by ~70bps, but the key Marmaxx division came in at +1%, a 500bps deceleration from +6%, and missed expectations of +2%. Q3 EPS guidance of $1.30–1.32 and comps of +2–3% were both below Street. FY26 EPS was raised to $5.31–5.36, but Marmaxx trends suggest competitive pressure from ROST, BURL, and TGT/WMT. Q2 results also benefited from $331M in IEEPA tariff refunds.

bullets.title: LOW cuts FY guidance on persistent DIY weakness; Pro holding up but residential construction headwinds persist
bullets.body: Lowe's Q2 comps of +0.2% missed consensus +0.5%, and the company lowered FY26 revenue guidance to $92B (from $94B) with flat comp sales expected. FY EPS guided to ~$12.25, down from the prior range of $12.25–12.75. Q2 benefited from one-time tariff refunds; no additional refunds assumed in H2. Pro and premium appliances are offsetting soft DIY demand, but residential construction headwinds are expected to persist through year-end. A consumer survey showed project spend fell ~10% from March to August with major kitchen renovations down ~one-third.

bullets.title: Moderna +100%+ on first-ever positive Phase 3 melanoma vaccine result; biotech sector broadly rallies
bullets.body: Moderna surged over 100% after its mRNA-4157 personalized cancer vaccine combined with Merck's Keytruda met the primary endpoint in the Phase 3 INTerpath-001 melanoma trial — the first-ever positive Phase 3 result for a personalized cancer vaccine. Merck jumped ~10%, BioNTech +19%, and Novavax +7% on sympathy. Health Technology sector dominated the 52-week high list with 61 stocks hitting new highs on the day.

bullets.title: Retail sector broadly soft: July retail units down 2% YoY, discretionary GMV down 4.3%
bullets.body: Hedgeye's retail data shows July retail units fell 2% YoY, with discretionary general merchandise dollar sales down 4.3% and units down 3.9%. Consumer spending is shifting toward smaller, self-funded home projects (vs. contractor work), with home equity financing nearly halved. Roth's home remodeling survey confirmed project spend fell ~10% from March to August, with HD losing market share to Lowe's as primary supplier.

bullets.title: Samsung Foundry hikes advanced node prices 10–15% amid full capacity; implications for chip cost structure
bullets.body: Samsung Foundry raised SF4 (4nm) chipmaking prices by 10–15% month-over-month in July/August for US and China customers, with the Pyeongtaek plant operating at full capacity since late last year. Chinese customers are accepting the largest price increases. Samsung is also redesigning its Pyeongtaek P5 facility from 2-story to 3-story to expand capacity. The price hike reflects broad semiconductor demand strength and will flow through to chip product costs.

bullets.title: Geopolitical risk elevated: Iran weighs striking US targets in Europe; China military exercise near Taiwan
bullets.body: Iran is reportedly considering expanding its target list to US military assets in Europe (including Bulgaria and Cyprus) contingent on further Washington escalation; NATO stated readiness to defend all allies. Separately, China deployed 20 warplanes, 7 warships, and 6 official ships near Taiwan. China also warned no entity should assist in implementing the EU anti-subsidy probe, threatening retaliation against the EU.

bullets.title: Oil and energy prices elevated: Brent/WTI up >1% to highest since late July; Saudi dark-sailing signals
bullets.body: Brent and US crude futures gained over 1%, reaching their highest levels since late July. Saudi Arabia offering oil sales near Oman suggests potential dark sailing of tankers through the Hormuz strait, signaling supply chain adaptation to geopolitical tensions. European gas prices remain supported by winter supply risks. US diesel crack spread hit a record $102/barrel with US diesel reserves at 23-year lows.

bullets.title: Goldman Risk Appetite at 99th percentile; BofA FMS cash at cycle low, equity allocations near multi-year highs
bullets.body: Goldman's Risk Appetite Indicator is at the 99th percentile, while BofA's Fund Manager Survey shows cash at a 3.5% cycle low and equity allocations near multi-year highs — classic late-cycle positioning signals. 96% of S&P 500 companies are in open buyback windows with over $1 trillion in authorized repurchases, running at 1.5x 2025 average daily trading volume. Factor volatility is elevated with over 20 one-day 5% sell-offs in High Beta Momentum year-to-date.
